newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST--Carso Q3 seen flat vs Q2.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST--Carso Q3 seen flat vs Q2.

text.p: Mexican conglomerate Grupo Carso SA is expected to turn in healthy third quarter results compared with the year-ago quarter, but profits are seen flat against the second quarter of this year, analysts said.
A survey of three industry analysts forecast a third quarter earnings per share of 0.71 pesos. Carso's first half profits were 1.555 billion pesos.
Carso has continued to tap into Mexico's export boom and has also benefitted from the slight recovery in the domestic economy, analysts said.
Higher prices for its cigarette business should help that unit's margins, while industrial firm Condumex's auto parts division should turn in a big jump in sales, analysts said.
Flat prices should hurt mining firm Frisco, while ongoing weakness in the economy will pinch retailer Sanborns.
"It should be a good quarter, especially for Condumex," said Kerry McHugh, an analyst at Goldman Sachs in New York.

Carso, Mexico's largest holding company, reflects a broad spectrum of Mexican business conditions. Its holdings include Cigatam cigarette company, Sanborns, Condumex, mining firms Nacobre and Frisco and tire company Corporacion Llantera.
Earlier this year, Carso also spun off its controlling stake in telephone monopoly Telmex into a new company focused on telecommunications and multimedia: Carso Global Telecom.
Prabhas Panigrahi, an analyst at CS First Boston, said he thinks Carso is well-managed, but wonders where the company's future growth will come from given its mature businesses mix.
"I don't see a growth catalyst in the near future or any areas that the company is considering," Panigrahi said.
He added the company's recent move to pull out of bidding for Mexico's soon-to-be privatized railroads was disappointing.
